item.title: Multiple types of bulk waste dumped near 57 HAMPTON STREET LONDON SE17 3AN, 12th August
item.description:
Large quantities of dumped household and bulky waste are present within communal areas and on pedestrian footways. Items include mattresses, broken furniture, timber, suitcases, bags of refuse, cardboard, electrical appliances and miscellaneous loose debris. The waste is obstructing access routes and encroaching onto areas used by residents and members of the public. The dumped items present several risks, including: Trip and fall hazards from loose debris, protruding timber, broken furniture and items left on walkways. Cuts and puncture injuries caused by exposed sharp edges, broken materials, nails, fixings or damaged appliance components. Entrapment and climbing risks for young children, who may be attracted to the mattresses, furniture and piled waste, increasing the likelihood of injury. Manual handling and collapse hazards from unstable stacked items that could topple if disturbed. Fire risk due to the accumulation of combustible materials such as mattresses, timber, cardboard and textiles. Pest and environmental health issues arising from accumulated refuse and waste materials. The waste requires urgent removal to eliminate the hazards and restore safe access through the communal area.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Hampton Street, Elephant and Castle, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: 5 cars taking up spaces in public car park, 12th August
item.description:
I would like to report five vehicles which appear to have been left for extended periods in this Bexley Council-owned public car park. The vehicles are: • SD55 HNN — has remained in the same position for at least six weeks. • LT58 ORS — has remained in the same position for at least six weeks. • EF18 VXW — has remained in the same position for approximately three weeks. • CU68 YBT — has remained in the same position for approximately three weeks. • YH59 WFY — has remained in the same position for approximately three weeks. As far as I have been able to observe, none of these vehicles has moved during these periods. Parking availability here is already very limited, and these vehicles are continuously occupying spaces for long periods. I regularly find the car park full when returning home from work while these vehicles remain in the same spaces. Could the Council please inspect the vehicles and check whether they are legitimately being kept in the car park, or whether they meet the criteria for abandoned vehicles or require any other enforcement action? I would prefer to remain anonymous. If my contact details are required to process the report, please keep my identity and contact details confidential and do not disclose them to the vehicle owners or registered keepers. Thank you.
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): West Heath, Greater London

item.title: Outside 27 Chalcot Crescent NW1 8YE, 11th August
item.description:
